in_arabic.name: حاتف

in_urdu.name: حاتف
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ کی طرف سے دی گئی خوشخبری یا مبارک پیغام
in_urdu.long_meaning: حاتف نام کا مطلب ہے اللہ کی طرف سے دی گئی خوشخبری یا مبارک پیغام۔ یہ نام اسلامی روایات میں اہم سمجھا جاتا ہے کیونکہ یہ الہام یا وحی کے تصور سے جڑا ہوا ہے جو انسان کو روحانی رہنمائی فراہم کرتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کے لئے، یہ نام پवित्र اور مبارک سمجھا جاتا ہے۔

in_pashto.name: حاتف
in_pashto.meaning: د الهي له خوا څخه د رارسیدو نیک خبر یا برکت
in_pashto.long_meaning: حاتف نوم د الهي له خوا څخه د رارسیدو نیک خبر یا برکت معنی لري. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ارزښتونو سره تړلی دی او د روحاني لارښوونې او الهي پيغام د ترلاسه کولو مفهوم منعکس کوي. دا نوم د پښتنو مسلمانو لپاره د پام وړ دی.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidaya wa Al-Nihaya: Volume 10, Page 481 The name Hatif carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The story of Hatif ibn Al-Asad who was a poet and a lover from the tribe of Asad. He loved and was loved by Umm Haram bint Milhan, the wife of the Prophet Muhammad. When the Prophet went to Medina, Umm Haram was left in Mecca. Hatif used to visit her while the Prophet was away. When the Prophet found out, he allowed Umm Haram to marry Hatif. However, the Prophet's companions disapproved and considered it a violation of the Prophet's rights. The Prophet then allowed Umm Haram to choose between him and Hatif. Umm Haram chose the Prophet and Hatif left Mecca.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Jamal's Al-Ansab: Volume 9, Page 242-243 The name Hatif carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The story of Hatif ibn Malik, a poet from the tribe of Tamim who was called 'Al-Mazhul' (the deranged) due to his love for Umm Salama, the wife of the Prophet Muhammad. The Prophet found out about Hatif's feelings and said to him, 'Do not be sad, for I am not in need of the love of a man who is not in need of my love.' Hatif was moved by the Prophet's words and became a devoted follower. When the Prophet later passed through Hatif's town, Hatif asked for permission to perform a ritual pilgrimage (Umra) to Mecca. The Prophet allowed him to do so and also granted him permission to visit Umm Salama.
